note: Questions that must be answered before a decision can reasonably be made. 'Answer now' states only what the verified files support. Status values: Answered (policy or verified fact), Partly answered, Unanswered.

items.question: Which games have verified official final scores in this project?
items.answer_now: 16 games: all 15 Week 9 games and the Week 10 Thursday game (Commanders 24, Giants 21). Three of them are also printed in official Game Books.
items.missing: Weeks 1 to 8 and the rest of the 2026 season; manual opening of each game-centre page; prior seasons.
items.how_to_find: Read each official weekly schedule page (2 to 3 chunks each), open each game centre, and store the page hash and read time in results_verified.csv.

items.question: Do we have opening and closing prices for any market we originate?
items.answer_now: No. There is one point-in-time DraftKings observation for eight Week 10 games (48 market rows). Opening and closing columns are empty. The capture time is unknown.
items.missing: Timestamped opening and closing prices from an archive or from our own capture before each kickoff.
items.how_to_find: Start a capture protocol (for example T-72h, T-24h, T-1h and kickoff, UTC-stamped) for each game, or license an archive with timestamps and settlement rules. Check the operator's jurisdiction first (Q10).
items.blocks: Market line, difference, closing-line value and ROI.

items.question: Can we publish our own fair line for a Week 10 game?
items.answer_now: No, not from verified inputs. Sixteen official results are too few to rate teams, and no model has been fitted or calibrated.
items.missing: A verified multi-season results history with as-of cutoffs, and a documented model with calibration on held-out weeks.
items.how_to_find: Collect official seasonal results for prior seasons, record provenance for each, fit a frozen model on earlier weeks only, and test it on later weeks.
items.blocks: Fair line, difference and every forecast-quality gate.

items.question: In what order are the markets originated?
items.answer_now: Side first, then total, then moneyline. The rule is written in policy.json and is shown in the lines table.
items.missing: Execution. No line has been originated under this order yet.
items.how_to_find: Not needed for the policy. Execution depends on Q03.
items.blocks: Nothing in the policy; execution is blocked by Q03.

items.question: What are the measured correlations between legs?
items.answer_now: Zero official paired observations exist for any of the eight predeclared pairs. n = 0 is published for each pair. No coefficient is published.
items.missing: Paired as-of observations (for example each QB's yards and each receiver's yards in the same game).
items.how_to_find: Extract paired player statistics from official NFL stats pages for each game; publish n with each coefficient.

items.question: Which strategies are eligible to rank on the leaderboard?
items.answer_now: None. All eleven gates are not evaluated, so no strategy is eligible.
items.missing: Evaluated gate results for each strategy.
items.how_to_find: Run the gate checks once Q01 to Q03 are answered.

items.question: Has any strategy been backtested with executable prices?
items.answer_now: No. A file in own9-research reports results at an assumed price of -110 on both sides. That is an assumption, not a market price (see F30), so it is not evidence.

items.question: Can we track starters being replaced and by whom?
items.answer_now: Partly. For Week 9 to Week 10 we track starter changes for Washington and the Giants from Game Books: 12 records, including one replacement chain (L.Patrick to N.Allegretti at centre).
items.missing: Full-season starter history, every week, and each team's inactives.
items.how_to_find: Read each official Game Book (or lineup section) for every game, and diff the starter sets week by week.
items.blocks: Deficiency and replacement-depth analysis across the league.

items.question: What depth tier (1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th string) did each replacement hold?
items.answer_now: Not published by the NFL in the sources read. Depth-tier columns are blank by rule.
items.missing: An official depth-tier source. Club depth charts exist but are labelled unofficial by the clubs.
items.how_to_find: Ask for or locate an official depth-chart feed with a published date. Until then, keep tiers blank and show only the chain and the injury evidence.

items.question: In which jurisdiction would any wager or cash reward operate, and is it lawful for the user?
items.answer_now: The user's location is unconfirmed: neither the user nor a source in this repository establishes it. The Penal Code (Articles 185 and 186) makes gambling an offence, with a narrow exception for stakes that are only temporary entertainment. The project's market and regulator sources are US-scoped. Whether any activity is lawful is a legal question this project cannot answer.
items.missing: A written legal determination for the user, covering the activity, the operator and any reward.
items.how_to_find: Obtain qualified Japanese legal advice before any wager, stake or cash reward step. Until then, keep the project to paper research.
items.blocks: Any staking track, reward or real-money step.

items.question: Is any reward funded, and is its schedule frozen before the competition starts?
items.answer_now: No reward is funded. No schedule exists.
items.missing: A funding decision, a legal review (Q10) and a frozen reward schedule.

items.question: What numeric demotion thresholds apply?
items.answer_now: The gate is defined (D1 to D6). The numbers marked PROPOSED have not been set by the owner.
items.missing: Owner choice of N_min, bin size, tolerances and the staking cap.
items.how_to_find: Owner selects one of the options in the suggestions page (SX05).
items.blocks: Automatic demotion; the gate cannot yet be applied to a number.

items.question: How are pushes, voids and ties settled?
items.answer_now: DraftKings rules say a two-way point-spread tie, or a total equal to the line, settles as a Push, and a two-way moneyline tie settles as a Push (DK-GENERAL, DK-MARKETS). These are operator rules from a Virginia snapshot, so they do not establish settlement for the user's jurisdiction or for any other operator.
items.missing: Settlement rules for the actual operator and jurisdiction used.
items.how_to_find: Depends on Q10 and the operator choice.
items.blocks: Settlement in any historical or forward ledger.

items.question: Is the third-party historical games file licensed for our use?
items.answer_now: Not confirmed. The file is in own9-research/data and data/raw; its licence and provenance are not verified (F23 and F24 in flags.html).
items.missing: The upstream licence and a checksum-linked provenance record.
items.how_to_find: Read the upstream licence and record the file hash. If it is not permitted, replace it with official NFL pages.
items.blocks: Any use of the file as a training or backtest source.

items.question: Who owns the decisions in this project?
items.answer_now: The project owner (the user). The board in COORDINATION.md records no decisions yet.
items.missing: The owner's choice on each suggestion in the suggestions page.
items.how_to_find: The owner records a choice (option ID and date) in the decision log on that page.
